messages:
Sam: FYI - observed hosted -> dedicated fallback loses prefix/KV cache and token latency jumps ~2.8x on a short repro. Repro payload attached.
Oliver: Seen the same on my perf tests. The fallback path appears to create a new session without attempting snapshot restore.
Mia: Are we switching model variants during fallback (quant vs fp16)? That would also change perf.
Sam: No variant switch, same model id/version. The runtime shows empty KV store after fallback.
Tara: We intentionally set preserve_kv_cache=false in the original handoff RFC to avoid cross-tenant state reuse. But we sketched a snapshot handshake to make safe restores possible.
DevEx: Quick note - customers are noticing quality regressions when cache isn't restored for multi-turn flows. That hits PLG uptake.
InfraBot: Canary rollout: hosted-fallbacks v3 -> 5 hosts. Monitoring enabled.
Oliver: Proposal: add capability negotiation in the adapter handshake: runtimeCapabilities: { accepts_crypted_snapshot: true/false, snapshot_version: "v1" } and only restore if accepts_crypted_snapshot==true and snapshot_version compatible.
Sam: Agreed. Implementation sketch: (1) adapter queries runtime capabilities on route resolution; (2) control plane prepares an encrypted snapshot token scoped to tenant+session; (3) adapter passes token to runtime which requests KMS unwrap; (4) runtime validates TTL and tenant id then restores KV.
Mia: Important: tokens must be ephemeral and tenant-scoped. Also log an audit entry on restore with a hash of the snapshot token (no raw secrets).
Tara: Security checklist: KMS envelope-wrapping, snapshot TTL (default 60s), anti-replay nonce, and explicit opt-in flag per-customer. Internal clusters may default to enabled; external customers opt-in.
Sam: For backward compatibility older dedicated clusters without the handshake should be treated as accepts_crypted_snapshot=false and get cold-start fallbacks. We'll include a rollout note and compatibility matrix.
DevEx: Can we expose a per-tenant flag in the Console so customers can opt-in and view restore audit events? That would help support.
Oliver: We'll emit metrics: fallback_attempts, fallback_restores, fallback_restore_latency, fallback_restore_fail_reason. Add tag: tenant_id_hash.
Mia: Test plan: microbenchmark cold vs restored, correctness test for KV contents (no cross-tenant leakage), KMS unwrap failure simulation, and long-tail latency under load.
Tara: I'll draft an RFC addendum outlining the handshake proto, threat model, and KMS flow. Include sequence diagrams and sample token format.
Sam: I'll open tickets: engineering task to add handshake and metrics (INF-812), a QA task for test matrix (QA-423), and a docs task to add opt-in Console flow (DOCS-120).
InfraBot: Created issues: INF-812 (handshake-kv-snapshot), QA-423 (fallback-kv-test-matrix), DOCS-120 (console-restore-optin).
Oliver: Rollout strategy: feature-flag the adapter handshake, canary on internal tenants first, then opt-in customers, and finally safe-default off for older clusters.
Mia: One more: snapshot_version negotiation so we can evolve the format. Handshake should return supported_versions list.
Tara: Agreed. Also include a migration guide for Dedicated operators with minimal steps to enable accept_snapshot capability.
Sam: Thanks. I'll prototype the adapter changes and ping folks for a 20-min sync tomorrow to unblock INF-812.
DevEx: I'll prepare a short customer-facing note explaining opt-in and safety properties.
Sam: Great. Meeting invite incoming. :thumbsup:
